Modal prices are neither guaranteed MSP receipts nor complete retail food-price series.

Missing reports are not zero arrivals; market unit and grade must be retained.

PDS allocation, lifting/offtake, distribution and household receipt are different stages.

limitations: Fetched snapshot lacks a reliable selected-date context and mixes day/progressive counters.
Some displayed ratios exceed 100%; do not call fraud or shortage without denominator, period and system-status reconciliation.
No dynamic amounts published as normalized observations.

title: Building resilient infrastructure for storage of food grains
publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
locator: Food Grain Storage Systems sections 1–2; PACS pilot; schemes
summary: Reports 8,815 cold storages with 402.18 lakh MT capacity as of 30 June 2025. Reports 917.83 lakh MT covered/CAP central-pool storage capacity with FCI and state agencies as of 1 July 2025. limitations: Capacity is not stock, annual throughput, uninterrupted operation or equal local access.
Cold storage spans horticulture, dairy, meat and seafood; total cannot be attributed to vegetables alone.
Announced, sanctioned, constructed and operational facilities require separate status; no complete village storage inventory verified.
Kisan SAMPADA PMKSY is distinct from irrigation PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana.

Audit-calculated levy is not proven theft, a court judgment, money recovered or a current 2026 loss.

limitations: Household figures are rounded to 0.01 lakh.
PWS-village households and all-rural households are different denominators.
Administrative connections do not establish regularity, quantity or water quality.
Delhi and Chandigarh are absent; no zeros are imputed.

title: National report on functionality assessment of tap connections, 2024
publisher: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation
locator: PDF page 18 fact sheet; page 49 quality methods; page 52 section 4.7; page 54 (printed 38), Table 6
summary: Survey covered 19,812 Har Ghar Jal villages, 237,608 households, 761 districts and 34 states/UTs. Table 6 publishes separate regularity, quantity, tested-quality and minimum-of-three index percentages. Section 4.7 explicitly says the sampling design cannot identify the same household fulfilling all three parameters; the published functionality index takes their minimum. Table 6 household-quality assessment uses microbiological laboratory testing and on-site pH; source-water chemical testing is analysed separately in the report.
limitations: Selected Har Ghar Jal villages are not all rural villages.
Published minimum index is not the observed joint share of functional household supply.
The Table 6 household-quality percentage does not establish full BIS chemical safety, including arsenic or fluoride; source-water chemical tests are a separate sample.
Quantity and quality have different sampling units; do not combine as household intersection.
Exact original publication day is unconfirmed; URL folder date is not used as publication date.

limitations: Use the underlying report's sample definitions and minimum-index method.
Published percentages are not universal village or household safety claims.

limitations: Safe is a groundwater extraction-stage category, not a drinking-water-quality guarantee.
Units generally mean blocks/tehsils/talukas/mandals, not individual villages.
National mean cannot describe every aquifer; extraction includes irrigation, domestic and industrial uses.
All-state numeric groundwater table was not recovered in this workstream.
